issues.failure_explanation: The form B is only T-coercive up to the compact perturbation -k^2(c u,v), so (vf) is Fredholm and may fail to be uniquely solvable for certain k (nontrivial kernel). The second assertion of Lemma lm3.2 (B(v_glo,w)=0 for all v_glo implies pi w=0) requires injectivity of psi -> pi psi - pi G psi, which reduces to uniqueness for (vf): if pi psi = pi G psi then B(G psi, w)=0 for all w in V, and one needs G psi=0. The cited argument from ye2024 is for the coercive-up-to-T Laplace case where uniqueness is automatic; here no hypothesis excluding eigenvalues k is ever stated, and the resolution condition only controls the tilde V part. The same unstated hypothesis is needed for the existence of u in Theorem glothm and everything downstream.

failure_location.quote: By using the contradiction and mimicking the proof steps in \cite{ye2024}, we can obtain that $\pi w=0$, then $w\in\tilde{V}.$

issues.overall_effect: Lemma lm3.2's characterization of tilde V, the orthogonality u-u_glo in tilde V used in Theorem glothm, and the error analysis all silently assume unique solvability of (vf).
issues.title: Well-posedness of the continuous problem is never assumed, yet Lemma lm3.2 (second part) and the existence of u depend on it
